Explain the example for describe the app in a manifest

blocks.text: A manifest is a JSON file that describes the app name, start address and display choices. A browser can use it when offering installation.

These examples belong in separate files on your own HTTPS or localhost site. Service workers need that trusted origin and cannot run in this site's sandbox. Use browser developer tools to inspect them.

blocks.title: Describe the app in a manifest

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `name` is the full app name and `short_name` is a shorter label.
`start_url` chooses where the installed app begins; `scope` describes its navigation area.

blocks.text: Save this as manifest.webmanifest. It supplies app details; a browser may need valid icons and other checks before offering installation.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: A manifest does not guarantee that every browser will show an install prompt.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Choose a short app name that fits under an icon.
